Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
In a directed weighted graph with |V| vertices implemented using an adjacency list, the worst-case single operation cost occurs when a vertex has the maximum possible number of outgoing edges, which is |V| - 1. For the amortized analysis using the aggregate method, we sum the total costs of all operations and divide by the number of operations to obtain the average per-operation cost.

* The worst possible single operation costs |V| − 1, because a single vertex in a directed graph can have at most |V| − 1 outgoing edges (one directed edge to each of the other |V| − 1 vertices).
* The average amortized cost of the sequence of |V| operations is |E| / |V|, since the total cost across all operations equals the sum of the number of outgoing edges of every vertex, which is exactly |E|, and dividing this aggregate cost by the |V| operations yields |E| / |V|.
